Reconfigurable wireless networks (RWNs) are being developed to meet the high-quality needs of various applications. These RWNs can dynamically adjust their physical properties to create a favorable environment for wireless communication. This research focuses on the reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology, which enables RIS to control the phase of reflected signals to optimize network performance. A new framework is proposed to analyze RIS-aided wireless networks, incorporating a comprehensive model that accounts for the impact of RIS on wireless signals. This framework is used to derive a closed-form expression for the outage probability of RIS-aided wireless communication systems, which is then validated through simulations. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in evaluating RIS-aided wireless networks and provide insights into the impact of key network parameters on wireless communication performance.

Our research presents an innovative approach to post-editing that leverages the
existing alignment between machine translation output and its source text. We
employ an advanced word alignment technique, which extends alignment to operate
at the phrase level, thereby facilitating the identification of broader
correspondences between source and target text. Experimental results demonstrate
that our extended alignment method outperforms basic word alignment in terms of
editing efficiency, and its effectiveness is further substantiated by its
application in a rule-based system for post-editing.

This study delves into the gravitational effects of Kerr-like rotating black holes within the framework of f(R,T) gravity theory. By examining the black hole's shadow and its energy extraction capabilities, we investigate the implications of this theory on observable phenomena. Our analysis reveals that certain parameter combinations can yield stable Kerr-like black holes with distinct characteristics, including a modified metric and a potential for novel physical interpretations.

A recent study of a neutron star merger in 2017 led to the detection of gravitational waves and a gamma-ray burst, prompting researchers to investigate the phenomenon through simulations. By leveraging the neutron star's cylindrical symmetry, researchers can utilize the cylindrical spectral method to model this event. The method, which has been successfully applied to various astrophysical problems, is particularly suitable for neutron star mergers due to their inherent symmetry. The research team employed the spectral code SRII to simulate the merger, utilizing the spectral method's efficiency and accuracy. The simulation involved a range of neutron star mass combinations, including equal mass, nearly equal mass, and unequal mass scenarios. The results showed that the cylindrical spectral method is an efficient and accurate approach to modeling neutron star mergers, particularly for systems with cylindrical symmetry.

The BaBar collaboration has conducted a study on the decay of the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ mesons into various final states, specifically the $\phi \pi$, $\gamma \pi$, and $\gamma \pi^0$ decays. By analyzing data from the Belle II experiment, a more precise measurement of the branching fractions for these decay modes has been achieved. The branching fractions for the $\phi \pi$ and $\gamma \pi$ decays were determined to be $(1.0 \pm 0.2 \pm 0.1 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-4}$ and $(0.9 \pm 0.2 \pm 0.1 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-4}$, respectively, while the branching fraction for the $\gamma \pi^0$ decay was found to be $(0.5 \pm 0.1 \pm 0.1 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-4}$. These results are in agreement with previous measurements and provide a more accurate understanding of the decay properties of the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ mesons.

This paper delves into the characteristics of fractal polynomials and their associated fractal spaces, particularly when applied to the Sierpiński Gasket. We establish a connection between the fractal spaces on the Sierpiński Gasket and certain closed subalgebras on the unit disk. Furthermore, we examine the fractal spaces' properties, including their representation in terms of integrals and a maximum modulus principle.

This research paper introduces a new approach to generating visual questions, called Guiding Visual Question Generation (VQG), which aims to create more informative questions that can be used to refine image captioning models. The proposed model consists of two variants: one that generates questions based on images and another that generates questions based on image captions. The information from these sources is then combined to guide the generation of more informative questions. The proposed model is evaluated on the VQA dataset and shows significant improvements over existing methods.

The relationship between the rate of energy release from supernovae and the formation of dark matter halos in dwarf galaxies is examined through a theoretical framework. A simple model is developed to describe the interaction between the supernova blast and the surrounding interstellar medium, taking into account the supernova's energy output and the interstellar medium's pressure. This model is used to investigate the conditions under which the supernova blast can form a dark matter core, and the results show that the core formation is highly dependent on the supernova's energy output and the distance between the galaxy's center and the supernova. A comparison with the results of a previous study reveals that the new model provides a more accurate description of the core formation process, and the results of the new model are in good agreement with the results of a previous study.

This research study examines the effectiveness of propositional preprocessing techniques in solving complex problems in higher-order logic. A key technique, HO-SAT, is presented, designed to handle a broad range of first-order statements commonly encountered in higher-order logic. These statements are characterized by the absence of quantifiers over variables that are bound terms. By utilizing a combination of propositional and higher-order constraints, HO-SAT enables the creation of a more efficient propositional representation of first-order statements. This approach is then applied to the field of combinatorial reasoning within higher-order logic, specifically within the context of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method yields significant improvements in the efficiency of higher-order logic solvers for a variety of challenging combinatorial problems.

The replicator dynamics in zero-sum games are known to always converge to a stable point, but in non-zero-sum scenarios, the dynamics can be unpredictable. This study focuses on the behavior of the replicator dynamics in 2x2 and 3x3 games, particularly looking at the presence of oscillations and chaotic patterns. It's found that oscillations in zero-sum games are typically periodic, but can be of the form of "relaxation oscillations" with irregular patterns. In addition, the dynamics can be chaotic in 3x3 games, with the presence of "strange oscillations" that can be identified through the analysis of Lyapunov exponents.

Random forest algorithms are a widely used machine learning method for regression tasks.
This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for understanding the behavior of
random forest estimates in a Bayesian context.
The analysis reveals that the distribution of random forest predictions at any given point
is characterized by a mixture of uniform distributions.
Furthermore, we establish a tight bound on the expected deviation of the random forest
algorithm from its true value, providing a significant improvement over previous results.
The bound's tightness is demonstrated through an exact calculation of the expected deviation
in a specific scenario, and we also derive a non-asymptotic inequality for the random
forest's mean squared error.

The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) poses a significant challenge to power grids due to the unpredictable charging and discharging patterns of these vehicles. To mitigate this issue, this study proposes a novel approach to optimize EV charging and discharging schedules in a distribution network, taking into account the impact on grid voltage levels. By applying a specific mathematical technique, the optimization problem is reformulated to facilitate solution via a specific algorithm. To ensure efficient and scalable results, the study employs a two-stage method that separates the optimization process into distinct time periods. Furthermore, the optimization problem is reformulated to accommodate the limitations of distribution networks, and a specific algorithm is used to obtain the optimal solution. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, the study conducts a numerical simulation using a standard distribution network model.

The orthorhombic structure of samarium orthoferrite is found to be thermodynamically unstable at room temperature, according to our research. The results of our study, which employed a first-principles approach, show that the orthorhombic structure is susceptible to decomposition into the cubic phases of samarium metal and ferric oxide. The decomposition process is driven by a significant energy release, amounting to approximately 0.18 eV per formula unit. The calculated energy values are in line with experimental data, which indicates that the orthocubic structure is metastable with respect to the cubic phases. The findings of our study are in accordance with previous research, which has shown that the orthocubic structure is more stable than the orthorhombic structure. The results of our study also support the existence of a significant energy barrier between the orthocubic and cubic phases, which is likely responsible for the observed stability of the orthocubic structure. The findings of our study are significant, as they provide new insights into the stability of samarium orthoferrite and its potential applications in magnetic materials.

The concept of niche is a cornerstone in ecological understanding, yet it's a multifaceted concept that encompasses both the ecological niche and ecomorphological niche. The former encompasses the range of resources and environmental conditions that a population can utilize and persist with, while the latter focuses on the specific traits and adaptations that enable a species to thrive in its environment. This composite concept is crucial for grasping how ecological and evolutionary processes interact and drive the dynamics of ecological communities. Despite its significance, niche theory has been underutilized in studies of community ecology, particularly in understanding the complex interplay of ecological and evolutionary processes within ecosystems. This paper aims to explore the underutilized niche concept in community ecology, focusing on its application in understanding the complex interplay of ecological and evolutionary processes within ecosystems.

This research presents a groundbreaking data-driven approach to designing optimal ventilation control systems in buildings, enabling the creation of virtual models that can be used to develop tailored, rule-based strategies. By utilizing machine learning and optimization techniques, the method generates tailored control rules that can be implemented on-site without requiring extensive computational resources. The proposed approach was tested in a real-world scenario, where it successfully created a data-driven model of a building's ventilation system and used it to develop a data-based control strategy that achieved significant energy savings. The results demonstrate the potential of this method to achieve near-optimal ventilation control without the need for complex optimization algorithms, making it a practical solution for real-world applications.

We have conducted a comprehensive study of the supernova SN 2019zqk, which occurred in the galaxy NGC 2770, using a combination of optical and near-infrared data collected from various telescopes. Our analysis reveals that SN 2019zqk belongs to the class of hydrogen-poor superluminous supernovae, which exhibit a unique set of characteristics. The supernova's light curve and spectral features suggest that it is a Type Ibc supernova with a peak luminosity of approximately 10^42.3 erg/s and a peak bolometric luminosity of 10^42.5 erg/s. Our analysis also indicates that SN 2019zqk is likely to have been caused by the explosion of a massive star, which had a mass of approximately 15-20 solar masses. Our study provides valuable insights into the properties of hydrogen-poor superluminous supernovae, which are thought to be powered by the interaction of the supernova ejecta with a circumstellar medium. Our findings suggest that SN 2019zqk is a member of a group of hydrogen-poor superluminous supernovae, which exhibit a unique set of characteristics, including a narrow range of peak luminosities and a lack of hydrogen emission lines.

The hysteresis characteristics of magnets are examined through a combination of theoretical models and simulations. The 2D and 3D magnets display distinct hysteresis properties, with 2D magnets exhibiting a unique hysteresis loop with a specific shape, whereas 3D magnets conform to the traditional hysteresis model. The hysteresis behavior of magnets is found to be sensitive to the distribution of magnetic properties, with a particular focus on the coercivity distribution. The hysteresis of magnets is found to be influenced by the presence of certain magnetic domains, with a unique hysteresis loop observed in 2D magnets.

This study investigates the influence of incorporating word concreteness as an additional feature in the induction of dependency parse trees. Our research examines the effectiveness of this approach in both dependency parsing and learning scenarios, where it is compared to traditional machine learning techniques. Specifically, we employ support vector machines and demonstrate that adding concrete words information significantly enhances the accuracy of induced dependency parse trees, while also allowing for the identification of semantically relevant features and providing insights into the nuances of word relationships.

Attribution methods for image predictions are often evaluated using human judgment, but due to the impracticality of collecting such data, researchers rely on synthetic data for evaluation. This paper explores the use of a pre-existing human attribution dataset to assess the reliability of image-specific evaluation metrics. A study was conducted to gather human attributions for 1000 image classifications from the ImageNet dataset, and these attributions were used to create synthetic data for evaluating attribution methods. The results indicate that these synthetic data can be used to assess the reliability of attribution evaluation metrics, but they may not accurately represent real-world data.

Researchers have recently proposed a novel concept of thin-shell wormholes with reflection-asymmetric properties, which exhibit similar observational characteristics to black holes. A comprehensive analysis of these wormholes is presented, focusing on their thermodynamic properties and stability. A thermodynamic framework is developed, and the first law of thermodynamics is shown to be universally applicable. A thermodynamic process is examined, and its efficiency is calculated. A stability analysis is conducted, and the results reveal that these wormholes are stable under certain conditions. A comparison with standard wormholes and black holes is made, and it is found that they share comparable stability and efficiency.

This paper introduces a novel inequality that encompasses a broader range of applications, including multi-particle processes, and examines multi-particle Fokker-Planck equations with complex interactions.

In the field of combinatorics, researchers have made significant contributions to trimer and dimer covers on various lattices, particularly with the introduction of the face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice in 1972 by Kasteleyn and in subsequent years with body-centered cubic (BCC) and simple cubic (SCC) lattices. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of these studies, with a particular emphasis on the mathematical underpinnings and techniques used to analyze trimer and dimer covers on these lattices.

We introduce Universal Domain Adaptation (UDA), a method that addresses both domain and label shifts. This approach utilizes a novel loss function, the Domain and Label Shift Loss (DLSL), to handle both types of shifts. The performance of UDA is demonstrated through experiments on datasets with label shifts, where it achieves comparable results to existing methods. Furthermore, by integrating UDA with a pre-existing UDA model, we achieve a 10% improvement in domain shift performance.

Reconstructing 3D object shapes from 2D projections is a complex task that can benefit greatly from the use of prior knowledge about objects. This paper introduces a new method called Diffusion Shape Inversion, which combines a 3D object reconstruction model with 2D image data. The 3D model is trained to generate a 3D representation of an object, and then uses the 2D image data to refine this representation. This refinement process is done using a technique called diffusion, which allows the model to iteratively improve the 3D representation by adding small changes. This refinement process is guided by a 2D projection function that maps 3D shapes to 2D images. The 3D model is trained using a technique called score matching, which allows it to learn the distribution of 3D shapes. The 3D model is then used to reconstruct 3D shapes from 2D images. The results show that this method can produce high-quality 3D reconstructions of objects, even when the 2D image data is noisy or incomplete.

Recent advancements in query graph ranking have shown great promise in tackling complex natural language questions. However, existing neural network-based ranking methods face significant challenges, including the need for a predefined query graph, the absence of a structured representation for complex questions, and the inability to effectively model the relationships between different question components. To address these issues, we introduce a novel end-to-end query graph ranking framework called QGA that leverages a graph attention network to automatically learn query graphs from natural language questions. QGA's innovative use of a graph attention network enables it to capture the relationships between different question components, and its ability to learn query graphs from natural language questions allows it to effectively handle a wide range of question types. Furthermore, we propose a novel question encoding method that takes into account the hierarchical structure of query graphs, and we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on four widely-used question answering datasets.

This research examines polynomial composites within various polynomial rings,
focusing on a specific domain, K[X, Y, Z], and its localized versions, where K is an
infinite field. The study investigates the algebraic properties of the composite ideal
(J+i), where J is a primary ideal of height two and i is within the ideal of powers
generated by linear polynomials. The research provides a detailed analysis of the
associated primes and secondary decomposition of these composite ideals.

Named Entity Disambiguation (NED) poses a significant challenge due to the scarcity of training data and the vast number of potential candidate entities. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that leverages the rich information contained in entity descriptions to enhance the performance of a Disambiguation Engine. This approach involves a two-stage process: first, a Disambiguation Graph is constructed to represent the relationships between entities and their descriptions, and then a Disambiguation Engine is applied to resolve the entities. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through experiments on two benchmark datasets, yielding superior results compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

We have calculated one-loop oblique corrections in a supersymmetric model with two Higgs doublets, specifically in the limit where the CP-violating phase is minimal. The analysis is based on the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model and includes the effects of the top squark and stops, taking into account the most recent measurements of electroweak precision observables. The results show that the MSSM can be consistent with current experimental data, provided that the stops are relatively light and their masses are well-separated. The analysis also reveals that the impact of the CP-violating phase on the electroweak precision observables is small, and that the MSSM can be a viable candidate for a supersymmetric model of particle physics.

We introduce a new approach for generating realistic new views of a moving scene from a single video recording, a task that was previously unachievable. Unlike previous methods, which relied on multiple camera recordings, our technique leverages cutting-edge 3D reconstruction and deep learning technologies to synthesize unseen perspectives of a dynamic environment. Our pipeline consists of two main components: a 3D dynamic model that captures the scene's motion and a novel view synthesis system that creates high-quality images from any desired angle. Our method outperforms existing solutions in both image quality and temporal stability, and we demonstrate its effectiveness through a thorough evaluation on various datasets.

We analyze a stochastic model for a fluid in a half-space, where the fluid's velocity is represented by a rough path, resulting from a specific type of rough differential equation. This equation involves a damping term that exhibits significant path regularity and skew-symmetry, and a control term that is bounded and smooth. Our research demonstrates that for a short time period, a unique solution to this equation exists and can be represented by a stochastic flow, and we prove that the fluid's velocity converges to a specific function as the rough path converges to a deterministic function.

This study investigates the properties of a randomly generated grain model, where the long-range dependence of its values at different points is a defining characteristic. The model is based on a compound Poisson process, where the intensity and scaling parameter are denoted by $\lambda$ and $\alpha$ respectively, with $\alpha$ being greater than 1/2. The study focuses on the behavior of the inverse of the intensity matrix as the intensity approaches zero, and its relationship to the properties of the random field generated by the grain model. The study establishes that the inverse intensity matrix converges to a specific, positive definite matrix, and that this convergence is linked to the properties of the random field. The study also provides a representation of the random field in terms of a compound Poisson process, and its implications for the behavior of the random field at different points.

Next-generation wireless networks will heavily rely on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) to enhance coverage and capacity. However, the massive number of passive RIS elements makes it challenging to optimize RIS configurations for efficient wireless communication. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel approach to optimize RIS configurations for reliable wireless transmission in a multi-user, multi-stream system. By leveraging a distributionally robust optimization framework, we develop a robust method to determine RIS configurations that ensure reliable wireless connectivity under uncertain channel conditions. Our approach is validated through simulations that demonstrate its robustness and efficiency in various scenarios.

This research focuses on designing a control strategy for complex, interconnected systems composed of numerous independent components. The control strategy is initially introduced as a centralized approach, where a single entity manages all components, and it is later extended to a distributed approach, where each component operates independently and communicates with its neighbors. The effectiveness of these control strategies is evaluated through the lens of large deviation theory, which enables the derivation of optimal parameters for both scenarios. The results demonstrate that the optimal parameters can be efficiently calculated using a method that scales linearly with the number of components. The research also provides a method for determining the optimal parameters for both control scenarios in a way that is computationally efficient.

Recent advancements in quantization have led to the development of highly efficient neural networks with minimal performance degradation. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have been particularly well-suited to low-bit quantization, with significant improvements in performance observed when using 1-bit weights and 8-bit activations. However, quantizing the activations of convolution operations poses a challenge due to their inherent non-linearity. To address this issue, a new technique called Convolutional Neural Network Quantization with Activation Reshaping (CNARe) is proposed. CNARe involves a novel activation reshaping method that can be seamlessly integrated into existing quantization frameworks. Experimental results on various image classification and object detection tasks demonstrate that CNARe can achieve state-of-the-art performance in quantizing both weights and activations.

A Type Ia supernova is a cataclysmic event that occurs when a white dwarf star reaches a critical mass, triggering an explosive nuclear reaction. This event can be initiated through several mechanisms, including the merging of two white dwarfs, a sudden increase in a star's mass, or a sudden increase in a star's luminosity. Scientists have long believed that Type Ia supernovae are a consistent source of light, but recent observations have revealed that the brightness of these events can vary. This variation is thought to be caused by the differences in the chemical composition of the white dwarf stars, which can affect the rate at which they produce light. This research presents a new theory that explains the origin of the brightness variations in Type Ia supernovae, based on the idea that the brightness of these events is determined by the chemical composition of the white dwarf stars. This theory suggests that the brightness of a Type Ia supernova is directly related to the amount of a specific element, called iron, that is present in the white dwarf star. This theory is supported by recent observations of the brightness variations in Type Ia supernovae, which show that the brightness of these events is directly related to the amount of iron present in the white dwarf stars. This research provides new insights into the nature of Type Ia supernovae, and may help scientists to better understand the evolution of the universe.

This paper delves into the online learning of deep neural networks, with a focus on non-linear models. It explores the relationship between the computational resources available and the complexity of these networks, with a specific consideration of how resource allocation can be optimized. A key contribution is the development of a framework for analyzing the online learning of deep neural networks, with a theoretical proof demonstrating how this framework can be applied to various network architectures. Furthermore, the paper provides a practical algorithm for online learning, with a specific consideration of how resource allocation can be made in real-time. A key finding is that, for deep neural networks, the optimal allocation of computational resources follows a specific pattern, with a focus on allocating resources to the lower layers of the network. This insight is supported by both theoretical analysis and experimental results, with a specific consideration of how resource allocation can be made in real-time.

The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a significant global health crisis, with over 100 million confirmed cases and more than 2.5 million fatalities worldwide. The sheer scale of the pandemic has strained healthcare systems, making it challenging to accurately track and test for the virus. To address this issue, a blockchain-based solution has been proposed, which aims to streamline testing and vaccination processes in the healthcare sector. This solution is designed to be user-friendly, secure, and efficient, with a focus on reducing the workload of healthcare professionals. By leveraging blockchain technology, the proposed system can provide a reliable and efficient platform for testing and vaccination, ultimately contributing to a more effective response to the pandemic.

Recent pre-trained language models have achieved outstanding performance in text classification tasks. However, utilizing these models requires a significant amount of labeled data for fine-tuning. In contrast, we propose a novel method for generating sentence embeddings that can be directly applied to text classification without the need for fine-tuning. Our approach involves utilizing a pre-trained language model to generate sentence embeddings, which are then used to train a linear classifier. Our experiments demonstrate that our method surpasses the performance of existing sentence embedding models, such as Sentence-BERT and Universal Sentence Encoder, and even rivals the performance of fine-tuned BERT models when sufficient labeled data is available.

We investigate how a specific type of quantum particle diffusion behaves in a multi-dimensional lattice, where particles can be in a state of being either present or absent. By analyzing the long-term behavior of the system, we found that its behavior is governed by a type of equation that is similar to a heat diffusion equation, but with a unique property that is influenced by the lattice structure. When the symmetry of the system is broken, the diffusion process becomes more complex and exhibits a type of behavior that is not seen in classical diffusion. By considering the effects of different types of interactions and the behavior of the system at different times, we found that the diffusion process can be described by a type of equation that is similar to a heat diffusion equation, but with a unique property that is influenced by the interactions. By analyzing the behavior of the system at different times, we found that the diffusion process can be described by a type of behavior that is not seen in classical diffusion, and that is influenced by the interactions. By considering the effects of different types of interactions and the behavior of the system at different times, we found that the diffusion process can be described by a type of behavior that is not seen in classical diffusion, and that is influenced by the interactions.

Theoretical analysis of the Kerr precession in a quantum Hall ferromagnet is conducted, and it is found that the primary factor influencing its attenuation is the interplay between the spin-spin interaction and the spin-orbit interaction. The findings are compared to recent experimental data.

We investigate the behavior of a conformal field theory with a conformal symmetry that is periodically driven. Our analysis focuses on two distinct phases of this system: a thermal equilibrium state and a non-equilibrium phase transition. We examine the properties of these phases and their transition point using a specific model of conformal field theory. We also explore the implications of this system for a quantum lattice model and its relationship to thermalization and many-body localization.

This research introduces a novel approach to sensor fusion that leverages multimodal generative models. The proposed method involves a two-stage process: first, a generative model is trained to synthesize a target modality from available source modalities, and then, this target modality is combined with the original sources to form a unified representation. The unified representation is then used for downstream tasks, such as object detection and semantic segmentation. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated on the Cityscapes dataset, yielding superior results in panoptic segmentation and object detection compared to existing methods, including those that utilize generative models.

A recent analysis of $B^0$ meson decays into a pair of pions and a neutrino or antineutrino has yielded a measured $C\!P$-violating phase of $-1.01^{+0.46}_{-0.49}$ radians, with statistical and systematic uncertainties included. This measurement is based on a dataset of 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 TeV by the LHCb experiment. The obtained result is consistent with the Standard Model prediction.

This research introduces the concept of Graph Symmetric Systems, a new category of distributed optimal control strategies that leverage graph symmetry. GSSs are designed to handle complex optimal control problems with multiple agents, even when the graph structure is unknown or changes over time. The proposed method builds upon the principles of graph symmetry and symmetry breaking to create an efficient and adaptable control strategy. The effectiveness of GSSs is demonstrated through a case study of the multi-robot formation problem, and the results show that the proposed method can achieve optimal performance with a reduced communication overhead.

This study focuses on the development of a labeled multi-Bernoulli random finite set filter, which is based on a modified version of the multi-Bernoulli algorithm. A key innovation is the introduction of a truncation criterion that enables the efficient handling of a large number of objects by disregarding those with minimal importance weights. This criterion is mathematically justified through the derivation of a bound for the total variation distance, which is used to assess the accuracy of the new filter in comparison to existing methods. A practical application of the truncation concept is demonstrated by adapting it to a multi-Bernoulli mean shift filter, which is then evaluated using a challenging tracking scenario involving multiple maneuvering targets.

Research into linguistic typology has been hindered by the lack of comprehensive and accessible knowledge databases.  Although recent efforts have made some progress, existing databases remain limited in scope and usability.  The primary obstacle to using typological knowledge databases lies in the absence of a standardized method for encoding linguistic features.  To address this challenge, we introduce a novel framework for creating a multilingual linguistic knowledge database that incorporates over 1,000 features and more than 2,000 languages.  The framework is built around a standardized ontology that enables the creation of a unified knowledge database.  We also provide an ontology-based ontology-to-ontology mapping tool that can be used to integrate existing databases into a unified knowledge database.  The resulting knowledge database is available for public use.

In reinforcement learning, off-policy evaluation involves estimating the performance of a target policy using data collected from a different behavior policy. A widely used approach, the inverse propensity weighting estimator, can be highly sensitive to the behavior model, particularly when it's inaccurate. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel method that mitigates the impact of model errors by incorporating a novel loss function. This approach, which we call the robust IPW estimator, is based on a minimax problem that can be solved using a dual formulation. We establish a theoretical framework for the IPW estimator, showing that it can achieve a significant reduction in error when the behavior model is misspecified. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed estimator outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

Biopharmaceutical manufacturing is a complex process that requires continuous monitoring and adjustment to ensure optimal production.  Model-based control systems have been developed to manage this process, but they are often hindered by model inaccuracies and limitations.  In this study, we address the challenges associated with model risk in a continuous fermentation process, which is a critical step in biomanufacturing.  We propose a novel approach that combines a data-driven model with a probabilistic framework to account for uncertainty and model risk.  The proposed method is then applied to a large-scale biomanufacturing process, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing model risk and improving process performance.

We have developed a new approach to study the properties of a large polaron in a three-dimensional environment, specifically when the interaction between the polaron and its surroundings is strong. By using a variational method, we have derived a precise mathematical expression for the polaron's energy-momentum relationship, which accurately accounts for the effects of momentum on the system's energy levels. Our results show that the system exhibits a unique behavior, where the energy levels split into two distinct branches, one of which is independent of momentum. We have also found that the system's ground state is unique and that the system's excitations can be described by a simple, linear relationship. Our results provide a new understanding of the polaron's behavior and open up new avenues for research on the properties of these systems.

We examine the electric field's lifetime in the context of strong magnetic fields, 
where we find that its behavior is influenced by the magnetic field's strength. 
Specifically, we demonstrate that its lifetime scales in proportion to the inverse 
magnetic field strength, in line with theoretical predictions.

We have developed a method for examining the properties of periodic arrangements by applying the concept of non-expansive lines to their projections onto their own dual space. This approach enables us to derive key insights into these configurations, including a new method for identifying the set of directions in which the projections of these arrangements are non-expansive. This discovery has practical applications in the fields of crystallography and tiling theory, where we have applied it to solve problems related to the crystallographic restriction and determining the range of lattice vectors for periodic aperiodic configurations that can be tiled with a specific set of polyominoes.

This article presents a novel approach to the metric space partitioning problem, a variant of the Borsuk problem. We demonstrate the existence of an upper bound on the Borsuk number for metric spaces with diameter D, by proving that the space can be divided into a finite number of subsets, each with a diameter not exceeding a specific value.

We establish that the resolvent of a specific fourth-order operator can be approximated within an error margin of $\varepsilon^5$ in H\"older spaces, with the approximation uniformly valid for $\varepsilon$ values close to zero. This fourth-order operator models the linearized stability of periodic shear flows in a two-dimensional fluid, as described by the Navier-Stokes equations. Our method involves a precise representation of the Green's function for an associated elliptic problem, which is then used to derive our result.

Recent advances in natural language processing have led to a significant increase in virtual assistants, yet most are designed for a limited set of high-resource languages. The lack of suitable training data in low-resource languages poses a major challenge for developing effective virtual assistants. To address this, we propose a novel approach to generate high-quality conversational data for low-resource languages by leveraging a large English language model. Our method involves creating a bilingual dictionary to translate English conversations into target languages and then using this dictionary to generate conversations in the target language. We also introduce a new metric for evaluating the quality of generated conversations. We test our approach on three languages, Hindi, French, and Swahili, and find that it produces high-quality data that significantly improves the performance of a pre-trained language model in the context of dialogue generation.

This paper presents an API for SMT solvers, offering a unified interface to leverage the strengths of multiple solvers in a combined approach. Our key contributions include a solver API, solver controllers that manage and coordinate these solvers, and a novel implementation of the API using the Python language. We demonstrate the practical application of our API by developing SMT-CDQ, a prototype system that combines multiple solvers and evaluates their performance on a wide range of problems.

This research paper explores the application of the path integral method to quasi-exactly solvable problems in one-dimensional space and two-dimensional angular momentum. It demonstrates that quasi-exactly solvable wave functions can be expressed as finite polynomials in one-dimensional space and exponential functions in a two-dimensional context. The paper derives integral representations for these quasi-exactly solvable states using the path integral method. Additionally, it shows that the application of the path integral method to harmonic oscillators leads to the same type of integral representations.

A significant limitation of CNNs is their inability to accurately classify images with low resolution. Research has shown that increasing the input resolution can improve accuracy, but this approach is hindered by the memory and computational requirements of high-resolution images. To overcome this issue, we introduce an innovative method that enables CNNs to classify images with minimal degradation in performance. Our technique involves dividing the input image into multiple smaller sections, which are then processed by a specialized low-resolution CNN. The resulting feature maps are then passed to the original high-resolution CNN for classification. Our approach has been successfully applied to various CNN architectures and has demonstrated improved performance on multiple datasets, including MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet.

We investigate the impact of spin state excitation on the surface of the binary asteroid system Didymos and Didyma, focusing on the potential consequences for the DART mission. Through thermal modeling, we found that spin state excitation can lead to surface temperature variations that may result in thermal cracking and thermal fracturing, potentially releasing dust from ExoMars' surface. This phenomenon could impact the laser ranging of the link between the two asteroids, but we found that the effect is minimal and unlikely to compromise the success of the DART mission.

A numerical method is developed to solve the linearized Einstein equations in the context of gravitational perturbations around a static black hole spacetime. The approach involves transforming the equations into a form that can be solved by a numerical solver, with the boundary conditions specified by the scalar field's regularity at the event horizon and asymptotic behavior at infinity. The method is then applied to a Schwarzschild black hole to study the behavior of gravitational perturbations in the near-horizon region.

The sensitivity of the DUNE experiment to sterile neutrino decays is investigated, with a focus on the relationship between the mixing angle between active and sterile neutrinos and the lifetime of a sterile neutrino. The analysis considers the impact of the neutrino's mass and its decay products, with particular attention paid to the effects of the neutrino's mass squared difference and the influence of the mixing angle on the experiment's sensitivity. The findings show that DUNE can detect sterile neutrino decays for a wide range of sterile neutrino lifetimes, with the experiment's sensitivity dependent on the neutrino's mass and mixing angle.

Recent breakthroughs in image denoising have been achieved through the use of deep learning techniques, particularly supervised learning methods. However, collecting large datasets of high-quality images with various noise levels is a significant challenge. In contrast, self-supervised learning methods have shown promise in achieving comparable results with significantly reduced dataset requirements. In this research, we introduce a novel self-supervised approach that leverages the inherent properties of images to generate a large dataset of clean images without the need for external noise models. By training a denoising network on this dataset, we achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple image benchmarks, including the BSDS100 dataset, and demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in real-world applications.

The goal of the k-sparse recovery problem is to find a k-sparse vector x from the Ax = y equation, where A is a given matrix and y is a known vector. A key area of study is the use of randomized algorithms for this problem, where algorithms are examined for their performance in terms of both the number of iterations required and the probability of success. A new algorithm is introduced that uses a specific random process to solve the k-sparse recovery problem, and it is shown to converge to the correct solution with a high probability. Furthermore, the algorithm is found to have a specific rate of convergence, and it is shown to be a special case of a more general class of algorithms for solving systems of linear equations.

Union and intersection types in gradually typed languages like TypeScript pose a challenge in verifying program correctness due to their ability to combine disparate types. This issue is addressed by the type system of TypeScript Fun, which incorporates explicit type checks for union and intersection types. This approach enables the use of type theory to ensure type safety, but current verification methods are limited to specific scenarios, such as the absence of type checks or specific intersection scenarios. This paper introduces a new method for verifying well-typedness in union and intersection types, using a type theory that supports a form of reduction. This approach is validated through a soundness theorem, demonstrating that well-typed programs are well-defined and consistent.

Reinforcement learning algorithms have shown significant potential in developing
motor skills, but their practical application in real-world scenarios is hindered
by the need for a large amount of data and high computational resources. To
overcome these limitations, we have developed a novel method that integrates
end-effect drives, a technique used in psychology to facilitate learning, into
the RL framework. By combining this approach with a technique called
off-policy learning, we have been able to significantly reduce the amount of
data required for successful motor learning. In our experiments, we have shown
that this new method outperforms traditional RL algorithms in terms of both
efficiency and accuracy, particularly in scenarios where data is scarce.

The concept of anharmonicity has far-reaching implications in various fields, including the study of heat transfer and the behavior of materials. In this context, we explore the effects of anharmonicity on an ideal gas, which can be described by a system of weakly interacting harmonic oscillators. By introducing a nonlinear interaction between these oscillators, we demonstrate that this interaction leads to a heat capacity that diverges, ultimately resulting in a phase transition. Furthermore, we investigate the properties of this phase transition, including the behavior of the heat capacity and the entropy of the system. Our findings reveal that this transition is of the first order, with distinct characteristics such as a peak in the heat capacity and a jump in entropy.

In the JT gravity model, we investigate the long-term behavior of certain correlation functions, specifically those involving the stress-energy tensor and the geometric operator. We focus on the AdS$_2$ black hole spacetime and derive the exact values of these correlations at late times, specifically for stress-energy tensor two-point functions and the geometric operator two-point function. The geometric operator function exhibits a non-decaying behavior, which is linked to the presence of a horizon operator in the dual conformal field theory. Additionally, we calculate the late-time correlations involving the stress-energy tensor and the geometric operator, which are found to be non-zero.

Social media platforms like Twitter are often the site of contentious debates, particularly around politically charged topics. To maintain order, Twitter implements policies to address content that violates its terms of service, including hate speech, harassment, and misinformation. During periods of heightened political activity, such as the 2016 US presidential election, Twitter has had to deal with a surge in reported content, leading to increased moderation efforts. This study focuses on the moderation efforts of Twitter during the 2016 US election, specifically the suspension of user accounts. By analyzing a dataset of suspended user accounts and their associated tweets, the research identifies the patterns and trends in Twitter's moderation practices. The study categorizes suspended user accounts based on their reasons for suspension, such as hate speech, harassment, and misinformation, and examines the characteristics of these accounts, including their user type, language, and engagement levels. The research also investigates the role of user reports in Twitter's moderation decisions and the impact of suspended user accounts on overall platform engagement. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of Twitter's moderation practices and the behavior of suspended user accounts.

This report outlines the physics justification for constructing a high-energy electron-hadron collider, specifically the e$^+$(e$^-$ p(p$\bar$ p)) collider, and presents a thorough examination of the physics opportunities, focusing on the areas where theoretical and experimental uncertainties are most pronounced. The report is a follow-up to the 2013 Snowmass report by the Electron-Ion Collider Study Group, with an updated discussion of the physics opportunities, particularly in relation to the Drell-Yan process, and incorporates the findings from the recent Tevatron and LHC experiments.

This paper introduces a novel dataset, called the "Houses Dataset," designed for classifying images of houses captured by crowdsourced participants. The dataset is notable for its inclusion of images with varying levels of quality, including those that are blurry or overexposed. Due to the dataset's noisy nature, two significant challenges arise: accurately classifying images and distinguishing between images captured by different users. To address these challenges, we propose a classification method that leverages a combination of a convolutional neural network and a graph convolutional network. The graph convolutional network is utilized to capture the contextual relationships between images, while the convolutional neural network is employed to extract features from individual images. The proposed method is evaluated using a benchmark dataset and demonstrates its effectiveness in classifying images of houses.

The 5G New Radio (5G NR) based cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) technology has the potential to provide more efficient C-V2X communication compared to dedicated short-range communications (DSRC). In this paper, we examine the performance of C-V2X in urban environments, focusing on the impact of interference from neighboring cells. We develop a closed-form expression for the probability of successful transmission in C-V2X systems, considering the 5G NR downlink control channel. We also derive the outage probability for packet delivery in C-V2X systems, considering the reliability of vehicular networks. We compare the C-V2X performance with existing DSRC systems and identify the key factors affecting performance. We propose a novel resource allocation scheme to enhance C-V2X performance, specifically the weighted round robin (WRR) scheme, which takes into account the channel conditions and traffic demands of vehicular networks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the WRR scheme through simulations and show that it can significantly improve the performance of vehicular networks.

Deep neural network models have achieved remarkable success in various AI domains, but their "black-box" nature hinders their adoption in critical applications. To address this issue, researchers have developed several methods for interpreting these models, but their effectiveness is hindered by the inherent complexity of neural networks. To tackle this challenge, we introduce a novel approach that leverages the inherent interpretability of linear models. By mapping the neural network's parameters to a linear model, we can extract meaningful insights from the complex model. Our proposed method, called Linear Interpretation, has been successfully applied to a range of image classification tasks, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10, demonstrating its efficacy in providing clear and understandable insights.

In collaborative software development, team members often work on the same codebase, leading to a need for temporary changes to facilitate collaboration. Feature toggles, a mechanism for enabling or disabling features, can streamline collaboration by allowing developers to collaborate without conflicts. However, managing and maintaining feature toggles can be challenging, especially when considering their impact on code quality and project management. This study investigates the usage of feature toggles in open-source projects, specifically focusing on their usage patterns, effectiveness, and potential issues. The research aims to provide insights into the challenges associated with feature toggle usage and identify best practices for their implementation. The study's findings can inform future research and practice in software engineering, particularly in the areas of collaborative software development and feature management.

In the context of 2+1 dimensional turbulence, the enstrophy current is a significant aspect of the dynamics. We have developed a generalized hydrodynamics framework for enstrophy in weakly nonlinear, incompressible hydrodynamics, which encompasses the conservation of enstrophy. We have also derived the enstrophy current and demonstrated its relevance in the context of the Reynolds stress tensor. We have successfully applied the enstrophy current to the Navier-Stokes equation and shown its role in the energy flux between different scales. Furthermore, we have shown that the enstrophy current can be used to describe the dynamics of the Navier-Stokes equation in the context of the Reynolds stress tensor. We have also shown that the enstrophy current can be used to describe the dynamics of the Navier-Stokes equation in the context of the vorticity current. We have also shown that the enstrophy current can be used to describe the dynamics of the Navier-Stokes equation in the context of the Navier-Stokes equation.

This paper presents a groundbreaking approach to processing massive point clouds by combining a unique network design with a hierarchical training strategy. Our method, which incorporates a hierarchical architecture, is paired with a novel training technique that enables efficient training of large-scale point clouds. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through experiments on large-scale point cloud datasets, achieving a significant improvement in accuracy and training efficiency.

A precise measurement of the muon's magnetic dipole moment, $a_\mu$, has been made, revealing a discrepancy between experimental results and the Standard Model's prediction. This discrepancy may be attributed to the influence of new physics beyond the Standard Model, potentially involving particles such as light scalar or vector bosons, or the influence of the Higgs boson. This study explores the influence of the Higgs boson on the muon's $a_\mu$ value, considering the possibility of a new light scalar boson, $S$, interacting with the Higgs boson and the muons. The study examines the effects of the $S$ boson on the muon's anomalous magnetic dipole moment, considering the mass of the $S$ boson and the strength of its interaction with the Higgs boson. The study also investigates the effects of the $S$ boson on the muon's decay into a Higgs boson and a muon-antimuon pair, and the constraints on the mass of the $S$ boson and the strength of its interaction with the Higgs boson.

Our research examines the impact of internal political constraints on international agreements, using a comparative study of the 1956 Suez Crisis and the 1990 Gulf Crisis. The analysis reveals that countries with fewer domestic constraints are more likely to negotiate a peaceful outcome. Furthermore, our study finds that countries with more diverse political factions are better equipped to resist pressure from aggressive allies. The findings are consistent with the theories of rational choice and institutional analysis, and we discuss the broader implications for understanding the relationship between domestic politics and international conflict.

The brain's neural patterns are capable of encoding intricate linguistic structures, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. A new study provides evidence that neural patterns can represent the hierarchical structure of language, as seen in the way they encode the meaning of words and sentences. This is demonstrated by the way neural patterns can be used to predict the meaning of words and sentences with a high degree of accuracy. The results of this study have significant implications for our understanding of how the brain processes language and could lead to new insights into the neural basis of language comprehension.

We've developed a new method to identify neutrino bursts from distant supernovae by analyzing the combined data from multiple Cherenkov telescopes. This approach leverages the coincidence of neutrino and optical detections, as well as the unique photon arrival patterns from supernovae. By using this method, we can significantly reduce the false alarm rate caused by background events. We've applied this method to simulated data from the Large Magellanic Cloud's supernovae and found that it can detect the neutrino signal with a high confidence level. Furthermore, we've applied this method to real data from the SN 2018bw event and found that it can effectively filter out background noise.

A new method for analyzing adaptive systems has been developed to study the impact of temperature variations on the wavefront, allowing for the identification of the most significant frequencies. The proposed approach, based on a Fourier analysis of the wavefront, enables the identification of the dominant temperature-induced frequencies. The method was tested on a high-resolution wavefront sensor and found to be effective in detecting temperature-induced disturbances. The results showed that the temperature-induced frequencies dominate the wavefront, and the system's performance is significantly improved when the temperature is stabilized. The method was also used to study the impact of the temperature variations on the image quality, and the results showed that the image quality is significantly improved when the temperature is stabilized.

Accurate predictions of lattice dynamics are crucial for understanding the properties of materials and designing new materials with specific functionalities. However, the computational cost of first-principles calculations is often too high to be feasible for large supercell calculations. To overcome this limitation, we have developed a machine learning approach that utilizes a neural network potential trained on a small dataset of first-principles calculations to accurately predict the phonon spectrum of a supercell. By applying this method to a complex material, we have demonstrated its effectiveness in predicting the phonon spectrum of a large supercell, which would have been computationally expensive to obtain using first-principles calculations.

We've developed a new approach to verifying termination in a broad range of systems, encompassing various types of models, including counter systems, Petri nets, and timed models, by introducing a new concept called "acceleration." This concept enables us to determine whether a system's behavior can be effectively bounded, which is crucial for developing a guaranteed termination procedure. Our method is built upon the framework of very-WSTS, which provides a unified framework for analyzing different system types, and we demonstrate its effectiveness by applying it to several types of systems, including Petri nets, timed models, and counter systems. Our results show that our approach can verify termination in a larger set of systems than previous methods, and we provide an algorithm for computing the acceleration of a given system, which can be used to determine whether the system is effectively bounded. Our method is particularly useful for verifying termination in systems that are not effectively bounded, and we demonstrate its effectiveness by applying it to several types of systems, including Petri nets, timed models, and counter systems.

The James Webb Space Telescope's launch in 2021 has significantly advanced astronomical research, particularly in the field of exoplanets, by providing high-resolution images of planetary systems. However, the telescope's images are affected by various factors, including the telescope's optics and the transmission of light through the atmosphere, resulting in blurred images. To address this issue, researchers have developed a new deep learning-based method to restore the clarity of JWST images. This method, known as the JWST Image Restoration Network, uses a unique approach to model the blurring effect of the telescope and the planet's atmosphere, allowing for the removal of blur and the enhancement of image quality. To evaluate the effectiveness of this method, researchers conducted a series of tests using simulated JWST images and compared the results to traditional deconvolution techniques. The JWST Image Restoration Network showed significant improvements in image quality, particularly in the removal of blur and the enhancement of image contrast. Overall, this method has the potential to significantly enhance the quality of JWST images, providing researchers with new insights into the planetary systems being studied.

A quantum system's evolution from a quantum state to a classical state is driven by decoherence, which occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings. This decoherence process, described by a stochastic master equation, is influenced by the system's density matrix and is typically associated with a stochastic process. This study explores a novel approach to modeling decoherence, which involves stochastic evolution of a quantum state's wave function, thereby allowing for the emergence of new forms of decoherence. This new approach is demonstrated through the analysis of a two-level system interacting with a bosonic bath, which is modeled using an open quantum stochastic process. This process, characterized by a specific mathematical formalism, is used to describe the system's evolution and is shown to lead to a decoherence process that is distinct from traditional models. This study also examines the implications of this new approach on the emergence of classical behavior in quantum systems.

This paper presents a method for determining the outer boundary of the geometric sum of ellipsoids, expressed through a simple, analytical formula. Unlike existing algorithms that rely on iterative processes, this formula offers a direct and efficient solution. Furthermore, it can be easily integrated into various optimization frameworks, such as sum-of-squares and semi-definite programming, to solve complex problems.

Recent advancements in deep learning have led to the development of deep neural networks that can learn from data. However, these models have been primarily applied to image, text, and video data. In contrast, the potential of deep learning for processing tabular data has been largely overlooked. In this research, we introduce a novel deep learning approach that combines the strengths of both classical and deep learning methods. Our experiments demonstrate that this hybrid approach outperforms traditional statistical methods, such as logistic regression, and even surpasses the performance of cutting-edge deep learning models, such as deep neural networks and gradient boosting machines, on a range of tabular datasets.

In this research, we explore the potential of transfer learning in machine learning applications for radio frequency signals. We examine the influence of various factors, including the number of training samples, the selection of the target domain, and the choice of model, on the performance of transfer learning. We also introduce a novel approach to transfer learning that utilizes the knowledge of the target domain's data distribution to adaptively adjust the model, thereby improving its performance. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly outperform traditional supervised learning and existing transfer learning methods in various scenarios.

We have used the Fermi-LAT's 12-year data to investigate the Milky Way's local dwarf galaxies for dark matter annihilations. By employing a novel method, we've incorporated the 12F catalog's distance and velocity uncertainties into our analysis, which has allowed us to constrain the annihilation rate of dark matter particles to various mass limits, specifically for the b-quark and tau-lepton channels. Our results show that the annihilation rate for a 100 GeV b-quark channel is constrained to a value of 1.1 x 10^-26 cm^3/s, which is a significant improvement over previous studies.

To improve search results in bug trackers, developers often need to incorporate specific terms from change requests. However, selecting the right keywords can be a time-consuming task. This paper proposes a novel method that utilizes a deep learning model to generate relevant search terms from relevant files in change requests. The model is trained to predict the relevance of files to a bug report and then extracts the most pertinent search terms from those files. The model's performance is evaluated using a dataset of 1,000 bug reports from the Eclipse platform, and the results show that the approach yields high-quality search terms that are more useful than existing methods.

This research paper introduces a new method for numerically solving complex fluid flow equations in porous media with varying properties across different regions. A novel approach is taken to create continuous numerical solutions that conform to the physical boundaries between these regions. To achieve this, a specially designed set of basis functions is employed, allowing for the solution to be represented as a combination of these functions. A critical aspect of this method involves determining the optimal number of these functions needed to ensure a continuous solution. To validate the proposed approach, numerical simulations are conducted and compared to existing methods in the field.

The task of summarizing conversations involves distilling key information from dialogue data, but this process is complicated by the inherent complexities of human interactions. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel approach that leverages the strengths of both abstractive and abductive reasoning to summarize conversations more effectively. By integrating a generative model that produces abstract summaries with a reasoning model that captures the flow of information exchange, our approach can produce summaries that are both accurate and reflective of the dialogue's underlying logic. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through a series of experiments on a conversational dataset, showing that it outperforms existing approaches in terms of summary quality.

The temperature dependence of the neutron-nucleus interaction is referred to as the temperature effect, resulting from the thermal motion of the target nucleus. This motion is described by a thermal wave packet, whose size is determined by the thermal de Broglie wavelength. This paper examines the temperature effect on the optical potential using a theoretical model that considers the thermal motion of the nucleus. It is found that the optical potential's dependence on temperature is relatively weak, with a magnitude comparable to the thermal de Broglie wavelength. This suggests that the optical potential can be approximated as temperature-independent, with a magnitude of around 10 MeV, for temperatures up to 1 GeV. This finding has implications for the study of high-energy collisions, such as those occurring in heavy-ion collisions, where the temperature plays a significant role.

A direct correspondence is established between $n$-Lie algebras and a specific subset of $n$-pre-Lie algebras, which possess a particular property. This paper explores the phase space construction of $n$-Lie algebras, leveraging concepts of Poisson geometry. Furthermore, the concept of $n$-pre-Liebrackets is introduced, which serves as a Lie algebra generalization within the context of pre-Lie algebras.

This research aims to maximize the average non-real-time rate for a cell-free massive MIMO system, taking into account the delay-sensitive users' quality of service requirements. To achieve this, we employ a stochastic geometry approach to model the system and develop an analytical expression for the sum rate for a given set of transmit powers. We then formulate the power allocation problem as a convex optimization issue and apply the stochastic gradient projection algorithm to find the optimal solution. The results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of overall system performance.

We examine the approximation of entire functions by sequences of translation operators. 
This investigation is driven by the need to understand the spectral properties of non-self-adjoint, second-order differential operators. 
In a specific scenario, we establish that a sequence of translation operators can approximate any entire function of a certain growth class. 
In a more general context, we derive a sequence of translation operators that approximates any entire function of a growth class. 
These results are then applied to analyze the spectral properties of certain differential operators, specifically the one with a complex constant coefficient and the Bessel operator.

We have developed a theoretical framework that quantitatively links the energy loss in disordered, densely packed collections of tiny particles to the degree of disorder within the system. This theory is rooted in a theoretical understanding of how the particles move and interact with each other, and it accurately predicts the energy loss in various types of particle systems, regardless of their composition. Our findings reveal that the energy loss in these systems is closely tied to the degree of disorder within the system, and this relationship holds true for a wide range of particle sizes and concentrations. Our research provides new insights into the fundamental principles governing the behavior of densely packed particle systems, and it has the potential to inform the development of new materials and technologies that rely on these systems.

Continual object detection is an emerging area of research that aims to tackle the challenge of adapting to new, unseen objects without forgetting previously learned information. Unlike traditional object classification, continual object detection faces significant hurdles due to the need to accurately identify objects at various scales and locations. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel framework called Re-Play, which utilizes a small, representative dataset to simulate new tasks and mitigate catastrophic forgetting. By leveraging a teacher-student learning approach, Re-Play effectively transfers knowledge from the teacher model to the student model, resulting in improved performance. Experimental results demonstrate that Re-Play outperforms existing continual learning methods, achieving state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets.
